blocks.prompt: 6. If \(x\) is very nearly equal 1, then prove that \(px^{p} - qx^{q} \approx (p - q)x^{p+q}\).
blocks.explanation:
"x very nearly equal to 1" means \(x = 1 + h\) with \(h\) very small, so \(h^{2}\) and higher powers can be neglected.
We must show both sides have the same value up to the \(h\) term.
Plan: expand \(x^{p}\), \(x^{q}\) and \(x^{p+q}\) as \(1 + nh\), then compare.
steps:
Given: \(x\) is very nearly 1.
To prove: \(px^{p} - qx^{q} \approx (p - q)x^{p+q}\).
Method: Put \(x = 1 + h\), \(h\) small. By the binomial theorem \((1 + h)^{n} \approx 1 + nh\) when \(h^{2}\) is neglected. Expand both sides and show they give the same expression in \(h\).

Left side
\[px^{p} - qx^{q} = p(1 + h)^{p} - q(1 + h)^{q}\]
\[\approx p(1 + ph) - q(1 + qh)\]
\[= (p - q) + (p^{2} - q^{2})h\]
Why: \((1 + h)^{p} \approx 1 + ph\), \((1 + h)^{q} \approx 1 + qh\); then group constants and \(h\)-terms.

Factorise
\[= (p - q) + (p - q)(p + q)h\]
\[= (p - q)\left[1 + (p + q)h\right]\]
Why: \(p^{2} - q^{2} = (p - q)(p + q)\); take out \(p - q\).

Right side
\[(p - q)x^{p+q} = (p - q)(1 + h)^{p+q}\]
\[\approx (p - q)\left[1 + (p + q)h\right]\]
Why: \(1 + nh\) with \(n = p + q\).

Compare
\[px^{p} - qx^{q} \approx (p - q)x^{p+q}\]
Why: Both sides reduce to the same \((p - q)[1 + (p + q)h]\).
blocks.final_answer: \(px^{p} - qx^{q} \approx (p - q)x^{p+q}\) when \(x\) is very nearly 1. Hence proved.
